author: devlin-moyer
body:
#### Main improvements in this PR:

As I loosely outlined in #188, this pull request

- Adds cpd25681_c0: 2-methyl-trans-aconitate [c0]
- Adds TK37_RS13115: acnD
- Adds TK37_RS13120: prpF
- Adds rxn25279_c0: 2-methylcitrate <-> H2O + 2-methyl-trans-aconitate, GPR: acnD
- Adds rxn25278_c0: 2-methyl-trans-aconitate <-> cis-2-Methylaconitate, GPR: prpF
- Annotates cpd01501_c0 with both cpd01501 and cpd24620 as seed.compound IDs

These changes fill the gap that currently exists in the 2-methylcitrate cycle, which allows the model to grow when valine is the sole carbon source (by providing a way for the model to use propionyl-CoA). Most of the 2-methylcitrate cycle is already in the model:

rxn00679_c0:
H2O (cpd00001_c0) + Oxaloacetate (cpd00032_c0) + Propionyl-CoA (cpd00086_c0) --> CoA (cpd00010_c0) + H+ (cpd00067_c0) + 2-Methylcitrate (cpd01501_c0)
(gap)
rxn03061_c0:
Methylisocitrate (cpd02799_c0) <=> H2O (cpd00001_c0) + cis-2-Methylaconitate (cpd02597_c0)
rxn00289_c0:
Methylisocitrate (cpd02799_c0) <=> Pyruvate (cpd00020_c0) + Succinate (cpd00036_c0)
rxn00288_c0:
FAD (cpd00015_c0) + Succinate (cpd00036_c0) + H+ (cpd00067_c0) --> Fumarate (cpd00106_c0) + FADH2 (cpd00982_c0)
rxn00799_c0:
L-Malate (cpd00130_c0) <=> H2O (cpd00001_c0) + Fumarate (cpd00106_c0)
rxn00248_c0:
NAD (cpd00003_c0) + L-Malate (cpd00130_c0) <=> NADH (cpd00004_c0) + Oxaloacetate (cpd00032_c0) + H+ (cpd00067_c0)

These papers ([1](https://www.microbiologyresearch.org/content/journal/micro/10.1099/mic.0.000604),[2](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0188130),[3](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1110/ps.072801907)) mention that some organisms that use the 2-methylcitrate cycle to catabolize propionate convert 2-methylcitrate directly to cis-2-methylaconitate in a single step with an enzyme called prpD, but others have a two-step process catalyzed by acnD and prpF. The GFF file annotates TK37_RS13115 as acnD and TK37_RS13120 as prpF, but no genes as prpD. [Some papers](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0188130) claim that the intermediate produced by acnD is cis-4-methylaconitate, while [others](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1110/ps.072801907) claim that it is trans-2-methylaconitate. ModelSEED has [cpd25681](https://modelseed.org/biochem/compounds/cpd25681) for trans-2-methylaconitate, but no ID for cis-4-methylaconitate, so I’m going with trans-2-methylaconitate instead of making a custom cis-4-methylaconitate metabolite.

ModelSEED only has two reactions that involve 2-methyl-trans-aconitate:

rxn25279: (2S,3S)-2-hydroxybutane-1,2,3-tricarboxylate <-> H2O + 2-methyl-trans-aconitate
rxn25278: 2-methyl-trans-aconitate <-> cis-2-Methylaconitate

(2S,3S)-2-hydroxybutane-1,2,3-tricarboxylate ([cpd24620](https://modelseed.org/biochem/compounds/cpd24620)) is another name for 2-methylcitrate (cpd01501). Since cpd01501 is already in the model in rxn00679, and ModelSEED doesn’t have an equivalent of rxn25279 that uses cpd01501 instead of cpd24620, I’m using cpd01501 in rxn25279_c0 and annotating the cpd01501_c0 in the model with both cpd01501 and cpd24620.

And here’s the connection to valine catabolism:
rxn01045_c0:
H2O (cpd00001_c0) + NAD (cpd00003_c0) + L-Valine (cpd00156_c0) <=> NADH (cpd00004_c0) + NH3 (cpd00013_c0) + H+ (cpd00067_c0) + 3-Methyl-2-oxobutanoate (cpd00123_c0)

rxn06586_c0:
Isovaleryl-CoA (cpd01882_c0) + Protein N6-(dihydrolipoyl)lysine (cpd16584_c0) <=> CoA (cpd00010_c0) + S-(3-Methylbutanoyl)-dihydrolipoamide-E (cpd14699_c0)

rxn07431_c0:
2-Methyl-1-hydroxypropyl-TPP (cpd14700_c0) + Protein N6-(lipoyl)lysine <=> TPP (cpd00056_c0) + S-(2-Methylpropionyl)-dihydrolipoamide (cpd02700_c0)

rxn01925_c0:
Isobutyryl-CoA (cpd00481_c0) + Protein N6-(dihydrolipoyl)lysine (cpd16584_c0) <=> CoA (cpd00010_c0) + S-(2-Methylpropionyl)-dihydrolipoamide (cpd02700_c0)

rxn01924_c0:
FADH2 (cpd00982_c0) + Methacrylyl-CoA (cpd02187_c0) --> FAD (cpd00015_c0) + H+ (cpd00067_c0) + Isobutyryl-CoA (cpd00481_c0)

rxn02949_c0:
H2O (cpd00001_c0) + Methacrylyl-CoA (cpd02187_c0) <=> (S)-3-Hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA (cpd03572_c0)

rxn01480_c0:
NAD (cpd00003_c0) + 3-Hydroxyisobutyrate (cpd00876_c0) <=> NADH (cpd00004_c0) + H+ (cpd00067_c0) + 3-Oxo-2-methylpropanoate (cpd00287_c0)

rxn00671_c0:
NAD (cpd00003_c0) + CoA (cpd00010_c0) + 3-Oxo-2-methylpropanoate (cpd00287_c0) <=> NADH (cpd00004_c0) + CO2 (cpd00011_c0) + Propionyl-CoA (cpd00086_c0)

rxn00679_c0:
H2O (cpd00001_c0) + Oxaloacetate (cpd00032_c0) + Propionyl-CoA (cpd00086_c0) --> CoA (cpd00010_c0) + H+ (cpd00067_c0) + 2-Methylcitrate (cpd01501_c0)

- [X] Selected `develop` as a target branch
- [ ] Any removed reactions and metabolites have been moved to the corresponding deprecated identifier lists

body:
### TL;DR

Changed expiration_time field from string to timestamp type in NFT marketplace tables to improve data consistency and query performance.

### What changed?

- Modified `expiration_time` field in `nft_marketplace_activities` table from VARCHAR to TIMESTAMP
- Added `expiration_time` column (TIMESTAMP type) to `current_nft_marketplace_token_offers` and `current_nft_marketplace_collection_offers` tables
- Updated model structs to use `NaiveDateTime` for expiration time fields

author: joshdavham
body:
Previously, if a `Card` was failed enough times, its `stability` could reach 0. This specically caused problems where the retrievability calculation could result in a division by 0 or even making the value of `stability` 'stuck' at 0 for future attempted stability updates.

To patch this issue, I made it so that, if the next value of `stability` reaches 0, then the `Scheduler` just keeps the previous `stability` value. I also added another unit test and bumped the patch version number.

Lmk if you have any questions

author: bmcnns
body:
This pull request adds support for warm start training in the PyOperon scikit-learn bindings, allowing users to call .fit() incrementally. This brings PyOperon in line with other modern frameworks like PySR and Scikit-learn, which already support incremental updates.

By enabling warm starts, users can continue training from a previously fitted model. It also allows users to circumvent the constraints of the callback method  #18.

This feature is particularly important for research scenarios where training without batching can take several days. With warm start support and horizontal batching, experiments that previously took up to 20 days can now be completed far more efficiently. A recent paper, ["A Survey on Batch Training in Genetic Programming", by Liah Rosenfeld and Leonardo Vanneschi](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10710-024-09501-6), highlights the potential of batching strategies for improving the scalability of genetic programming.

The underlying support for warm starts was added in a corresponding pull request to the Operon core library, and this PR ensures that the Python bindings can take full advantage of that functionality.

This also addresses a feature request in PyOperon #22.

release notes 
# Merged PRs

## dolt

* [9089](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9089): refactor: use the built-in max/min to simplify the code
  Contribution: https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9044
* [9084](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9084): [no release notes] Handle NULL adaptive values
  NULL Adaptive values weren't being properly handled in all codepaths. Some operations during tuple building (such as trying to move them out of band) caused a panic. This fixes that and adds tests.
* [9083](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9083): Support for non-MySQL query elements during merge
  During the merge operation, Dolt creates a `CREATE TABLE` statement for the table being merged, parses it, and uses that information during the merge. This PR allows this process to work with a non-MySQL dialect.
* [9075](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9075): Don't alter branch head outside of transactions when amending a commit
  Fixes: https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9072
* [9071](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9071): Fix typo mistake of commmitted
  Thanks to @jbampton 
* [9067](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9067): go: sqle/dprocedures: Implement operational inspection hook, dolt_thread_dump stored procedure.
* [9066](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9066): go/store/nbs: Add info level logging for a store conjoin.
* [9044](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9044): refactor: use the built-in max/min to simplify the code
  Use the built-in max/min from the standard library in Go 1.21 to simplify the code.  https://pkg.go.dev/builtin@go1.21.0#max
* [9013](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9013): Add Adaptive Inline encoding
  Adaptive Inline encoding refers to values that can be stored either inline in a table, or out-of-band in external storage. Postgres calls them TOAST (The Oversized-Attribute Storage Technique) types.
  This PR adds two new encoding types: one for toasted TEXT columns and one for toasted BLOB columns.
  The important parts of this PR are:
  - The new encoding values `StringToastEnc` and `BytesToastEnc`
  - The `ToastValue` type: this type has methods for creating and inspecting TOAST values.
  - The changes to `prolly.PutField` and `prolly.GetField` to handle writing reading and writing these encodings to tuples
  - The changes to `TupleBuilder`, which choose an inline or outlined representation for each value with a TOAST encoding. It prefers to store these values inline, but selectively outlines columns in a deterministic way if the length of the tuple would otherwise exceed a threshold. (Currently 2KB, not currently configurable.)
  It is not currently possible to use these encodings in Dolt proper. For testing purposes, a variable `schema.UseToastTypes` has been added. Setting this variable to true will cause Dolt to use these toast encodings for TEXT and BLOB columns instead of the normal address encodings.

## go-mysql-server

* [2927](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2927): Converting a nil value should return nil, not panic.
  Most uses of `convertValue` checked if the input was nil, but `Binary.Eval` didn't.
  NULL should always be converted to NULL, so we can just put the check there.
* [2926](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2926): Provide a SchemaFormatter interface to complement the SqlParser interface
  Dolt uses functions in the sql package to create and then parse CREATE TABLE statements as part of the merge process. Therefore, we need the ability to create these statements for other dialects, just as we do for MySQL.
  This PR also exposes a Noop auth method for the same use case.
* [2924](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2924): fix ifnull typing
  fixes https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9076
* [2923](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2923): fix `AND` optimization
  This PR fixes `AND` optimizations where `TRUE & x` -> `x`.
  Probably should've seen this coming given our bug fix with `OR` [here](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2921),
  fixes: https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9074
* [2921](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2921): fix not equal conversions
  fixes: https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9052
* [2913](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2913): insert trigger bugs
  fixes: https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9039
  Inserts nested inside triggers is a special case that we have minimal testing for. Some of the things that were broken before:
  - we did not prepend nodes inside trigger->insert blocks, so `new` columns were not accessible / the index offsets estimated based on prepending trigger rows were invalid
  - subqueries inside trigger->insert that have no outer visibility did not make exceptions for trigger rows, which act like lateral rows
  - prepending rules are flaky and mistakenly prepended in-between project->project nodes
* [2893](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2893): Add Wrapper values
  This PR adds support for `Wrapper` values, a new type of value that the storage layer can provide to the engine. This is a generalization of the existing `JsonWrapper` interface, but is not limited to JSON values.
  Wrapper types are useful because they can represent a value in storage without needing to fully deserialize that value for the engine. The primary use case is for "out-of-band" storage values, such as large `BLOB` or `TEXT` values that aren't stored directly in tables.
  The Wrapper interface has the following methods:
  `Unwrap/UnwrapAny` - These methods both deserialize the wrapped value and return it. `UnwrapAny` returns an `interface{}`, while `Unwrap` has a parameterized return type. The implementation is encouraged to cache this value.
  `IsExactLength` - Returns true if the size of the value can be known without deserializing it.
  `MaxByteLength` - The length of the value in bytes. If `IsExactLength` is true, this is the exact length of the value. Otherwise, it's an upper bound on the length of the value, determined by the schema of the table the value was read from.
  `Compare` - Some Wrapper implementations may be able to compare wrapped values without needing to deserialize them. This method returns a boolean indicating whether or not this "short-circuit" comparison is possible, and an int indicating the result of the comparison.


# Closed Issues

* [9072](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9072): Potential concurrency Issue with `call dolt_commit('--amend')`
* [9076](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9076): Unexpected type conversion in IFNULL
* [9074](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9074): Incorrect optimization of AND operation in expression in WHERE clause
* [9052](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9052): Incorrect optimization of OR operation in expression in WHERE clause
* [9039](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9039): Trigger LEFT_JOIN indexing error

body:
This change groups the tests for redacting passwords in URLs into a single test function with multiple test cases. It also uses the `protocmp` and `go-cmp` packages to compare BuildEvents.

In general, I'd like one test function per _kind_ of secret we're redacting (such as passwords in URLs, non-allowed environment variables, or repo credentials) with one test case per _place_ where a secret could appear.

This way, if we find we're failing to redact a particular _kind_ of secret, we can add or modify the test cases for that _kind_ of secret and know we've covered it. Same goes for cases where we're over-redacting.

If people approve of this approach, I'll keep going!

author: arsu4ka
body:
This pull request fixes issue when unsigned transaction is being marshalled, which causes serialized output to be invalid. This happens because transaction can't have 0 signatures, thus if you want to serialize yet unsigned transaction you have to add dummy signatures to it.

There are two ways of fixing this issue:
1. **Strict approach:** return an error when unsigned transaction is being serialized.
2. **Soft approach** (_introduced in this PR_): Spawn dummy signatures to the length of `tx.Message.Header.NumRequiredSignatures`, accounting for those signatures that already exist

It is possible to combine both approaches by allowing user to select whether he wants to verify signatures when serializing transaction, but it'd mean making a breaking change since that option has to be specified in `Transaction` struct properties or be passed to `MarshalBinary()` method. Therefore, only one of two approaches had to be picked.

**Soft approach** seemed to be a better pick, since it's a widely used practice in _Solana_ ecosystem to build, serialize and send transactions through the network before they are signed. It's rarely the case when somebody forgets to sign a transaction and submits it to the network, especially when such things as `sigVerify` (during transaction simulation) exist. Moreover, the same approach (though a little bit different) is implemented in `@solana/web3.js` (https://github.com/solana-labs/solana-web3.js/blob/4e9988cfc561f3ed11f4c5016a29090a61d129a8/src/transaction/versioned.ts#L36)

=====================================================================

Second commit is basically a code optimization of `Message.MarshalV0()`, which made possible by the following Go rules:

- `len()` of a nil array = 0
- `:= range` of a nil array produces zero iterations

author: zbruennig
body:
A polish to the game's autocasting system released today, 2025-04-09. Full details are available [here](https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/a=13/farming--autocast-qol-improvements?oldschool=1), but I've enumerated the changes relevant to this plugin:

- Reduced magic level / running out of runes, and performing a combat action afterwards (typically a melee) no longer unsets the current autocast varbit.
- An autocast can be set without having the proper runes / level requirements.
- Varbit remains even when changing to a different weapon which can autocast, but not on the current spellbook.
- Varbit remains even between sessions, meaning the plugin should read all this on login (first login on the client especially) and correctly interpret the state. Game data is loaded in stages, e.g. the autocasting varbit is set first, before inventory and equipment is known. The plugin currently will hit a null pointer and crash.

Other than the login issue, which is fixed by adding another null check, most of these are fixed by removing assumptions. For example, if the autocasting varbit is set and we read an equipment change event, we were assuming then you had the level and runes to cast and set flags accordingly. We can no longer do this; state updates need to happen only by the relevant events.

All that to say, these were resolvable with two fixes.

I also updated the build.gradle because mine was out of date and not reading imports correctly. New version is directly from the plugin hub's latest template.

body:
This PR improves the network traffic graph widget in the Debug window to provide:
1. Multiple time range options (from 5 minutes to 28 days)
2. Data persistence between sessions
3. Interactive visualization features including tooltips and logarithmic scaling

## Motivation
The existing network traffic graph has limited utility with its fixed time range and lack of historical data preservation. This enhancement allows users to:
- Analyze network traffic patterns over different timeframes
- Preserve historical traffic data between session restarts
- Interact with the graph to get specific data points
- Better visualize varying traffic volumes with logarithmic scaling

These improvements are valuable for:
- Network debugging and troubleshooting
- Understanding Bitcoin Core's network behaviour
- Monitoring traffic patterns for optimization
- Research purposes

## Implementation
The implementation preserves all existing functionality while adding new features:
- Added a pre-configured timeframe selection (13 different timeframes)
- Implemented traffic data serialization and deserialization
- Enhanced the visualization with interactive features
- Improved tooltip information with precise timestamps and traffic rates

Supporting changes:
- Added formatBytesps function for a prettier display of traffic rates
- Added FormatISO8601Time for better time display

## Testing
Tested on Linux with various network conditions. The new functionality can be exercised by:
1. Using the slider (or arrow keys) to select different time ranges
2. Restarting the application to verify data persistence
3. Clicking on the graph to toggle between linear and logarithmic scales
4. Hovering over data points to view detailed information

## Documentation
The changes are mostly self-documenting through the UI and are constrained to the Qt interface without affecting core functionality.

## Compatibility
This PR maintains compatibility with existing functionality. The data persistence file uses proper serialization versioning to allow for future format changes if needed.

author: jagerman
body:
This PR refactors how storage server tracks the contact information (ip, port, pubkeys) of network nodes and how it initiates contacts with other nodes on the network.

In particular, this aims to make new swarm joining more reliable: currently there are known issues where new swarm members are not receiving initial swarm messages because the other swarm members can send the data to the new node before the new node is ready to recognize them as members.

This reworks the mechanism:

When a new swarm member is detected, existing swarms members now send periodic (new) "snode.data_ready" requests to the new member(s), and do not attempt to push swarm data to that member until they get back a successful reply (thus indicating that we can reach the node, and that the node properly recognizes us as a swarm peer).  Previously members would attempt to push pretty much right away, but there are various ways the new node might either be unreachable, or might reject messages from a node it doesn't recognize.

If the command times out, or the remote returns anything other than "OK", the new member is returned to the queue and contact will be reattempted after another ~30s.

Once the OK is received, existing swarm members then push swarm messages to the new member via the existing snode.data endpoint for the new member to load the data.

All of this only applies if the remote has broadcast (via uptime proofs) that it is running a new enough storage server to support the handshake endpoint.

(This is not a perfect solution, and there are still various issues remaining, but this is a stop-gap while we also develop a more robust, active syncing mechanism).

Along the way this ends up touching a lot of other code:

- the "Swarms" class had a very confused triple purpose of tracking the current swarm, tracking all snodes, and tracking contact info, and was confusing to use.  These three purposes are now in three separate (though related) classes:
  - Swarm tracks the current swarm info, i.e. current swarm members.
  - Network tracks the global service node state, i.e. can look up which swarm a user pubkey or service node pubkey belongs to.
  - Contacts tracks the contact info of all registered service nodes, regardless of their state (aside from being registered).
  - sn_record is gone, and it *somewhat* replaced with a contact.  This isn't a direct replacement, though: many places that previously had a sn_record now simply take a legacy_pubkey, and look up the contact when needed via the Contacts object rather than passing the contact around.

- Storage server now subscribes to address updates from oxend (using https://github.com/oxen-io/oxen-core/pull/1820), so that it can update the contact info for a node immediately when a proof updates it, rather than only doing it when new blocks come in (which can be 2 minutes old during normal times, and much longer if there is a chain delay).

- We now fetch all SNs from oxend (previously only fully-funded ones): this lets us set up contacts and permissions for partially funded nodes, even though they aren't yet in any swarm, but then we are more likely to have them ready to go as soon as they get fully funded.

- Bump oxen-mq required version to 1.2.19, for an update that rechecks SN state on each command, rather than only when establishing a new connection.

- Replace all remaining std::stringstream usage with fmt.

- Changed the legacy_keypair (and similar for ed, x) from a std::pair typedef to a standalone struct with `.pub` and `.sec` members.  The plain pair was a bit dangerous because it wasn't immediately obvious whether .first was the pubkey or the privkey.  This also pushes it into some places that were still taking them as two separate arguments.
  - Related change: we now initialize from oxend with keypairs instead of just secret keys as we just had to compute all the pubkeys elsewhere anyway, so easier to just compute the pubkeys as soon as we get the secret keys.

- Added `load_from_bytes`/`load_from_hex` member functions to key types, and added `[[nodiscard]]` to the static `from_bytes`/`from_hex`. Previously it was easy to accidentally use `instance.from_hex(...)` which just calls the static method and doesn't actually change `instance`.

- Removed some string helper functions that are trivial now that we have fmt, added `get_human_readable_bytes` from oxen-core.

- Made the "random tests per tick" into a variable so that it can be changed easily later; previously the code was only ever trying 1.

- Replaced bt_list serialization with a more efficient bt_list_producer, along with a hack that lets us extract the final version-byte-prefixed string without needing extra allocations/copies.

- Remove the exclusive transaction from the save_bulk call (which was locked multiple times over): there doesn't seem to be any reason why this needs to be exclusive, blocking out other endpoints while the data gets loaded (which might be length as we could have 9MB of data to insert).

- Add some code documentation to better describe why we do what we do during swarm dissolution and new network swarms.

- Fetch the remote's storage server version information from oxend so that we can detect when the remote has updated to enable the handshake process.

- Removes version gates for old features that are always supported now.

This PR is part of the work to publish grpc-gateway in [BCR](https://registry.bazel.build/), described in this [issue](https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/issues/5183).

#### Have you read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)?

Yes

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

This PR seeks to add the required files for the [publish-to-bcr](https://github.com/bazel-contrib/publish-to-bcr/tree/main) plugin, which will publish the gRPC Gateway project as a module in the [Bazel Central Registry](https://registry.bazel.build/).

The plugin aims to eliminate a manual publishing process for the module and initiate the process when a release is created.

The configuration consists of three files placed in the `.bcr` directory:

* `.bcr/metadata.template.json`: that describes the repository and maintainers' information.
* `.bcr/presubmit.yml`: describes the targets that will be built and tested on specific platforms and bazel versions to test the module. 
* `.bcr/source.template.json`: that will automatically substitute values for the repository, owner, and tag based on the repository and release data.

The final result of this process is the creation of a PR in the BCR repository to publish the released version.

#### Other comments

Once this configuration is added to the repo, the `publish-to-bcr` should be configured as described [here](https://github.com/bazel-contrib/publish-to-bcr/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file#how-it-works).

___

CC: @AlejoAsd for awareness.

author: roomrys
body:
### Description
This PR examines the use of a `sleap.nn` class in the GUI code, i.e. `TrainingJobConfig`'s role/use in `LossViewer`.

We find that the `LossViewer` only uses the `TrainingJobConfig` for its `TrainingJobConfig.optimization.early_stopping.plateau_patience` and `TrainingJobConfig.optimization.early_stopping.plateau_min_delta`. 

While it is convenient to pass in a single `TraningJobConfig` and then have `LossViewer` extract these parameters, since there are only two parameters being used, passing these values straight into the `LossViewer` isn't such a big ask. Moreover, we only call `LossViewer.reset` (where the `TrainingJobConfig` is passed in) in one place.

author: kpeez
body:
This pull request introduces significant changes to the `app.py` and `paperchat` modules to support multiple AI model providers. The changes include refactoring the code to use a common interface for different providers, adding support for the Anthropic provider, and updating the configuration and initialization processes.

Support for multiple AI model providers:

* [`app.py`](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959L6-R15): Replaced specific OpenAI client calls with a generic `get_client` function that supports multiple providers. Updated session initialization to include provider settings and modified API key checks to be provider-specific. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959L6-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959L53-R64) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959L74-R81)
* [`paperchat/llms/common.py`](diffhunk://#diff-974685d40b1e01e4212eae2b36f5145351418b74e23e92ed869e51308cbdb5c1R1-R199): Introduced a common interface for LLM providers, including functions for getting clients, generating responses, and listing models. Registered OpenAI and Anthropic as available providers.

Anthropic provider implementation:

* [`paperchat/llms/anthropic.py`](diffhunk://#diff-0a668a7e69a6e2277476f1eec90e8688b28d2054581e0d61ca596cff4227075dR1-R100): Added the implementation for the Anthropic provider, including functions for getting clients, building prompts, and generating responses (both standard and streaming).

Refactoring and cleanup:

* [`paperchat/llm.py`](diffhunk://#diff-8c5682d8eaa75e31489026f111446e5ddf771892c1f43ff4e8283142d4e4bef1L4-L137): Removed OpenAI-specific code and replaced it with calls to the common interface. Updated function signatures to include the provider name parameter. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8c5682d8eaa75e31489026f111446e5ddf771892c1f43ff4e8283142d4e4bef1L4-L137) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8c5682d8eaa75e31489026f111446e5ddf771892c1f43ff4e8283142d4e4bef1L147-R33) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8c5682d8eaa75e31489026f111446e5ddf771892c1f43ff4e8283142d4e4bef1R47) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-8c5682d8eaa75e31489026f111446e5ddf771892c1f43ff4e8283142d4e4bef1R57) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-8c5682d8eaa75e31489026f111446e5ddf771892c1f43ff4e8283142d4e4bef1L195-R74) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-8c5682d8eaa75e31489026f111446e5ddf771892c1f43ff4e8283142d4e4bef1L209-R100) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-8c5682d8eaa75e31489026f111446e5ddf771892c1f43ff4e8283142d4e4bef1R127)
* [`paperchat/llms/openai.py`](diffhunk://#diff-1f78b21e960a35ada0d72cf73e82d428ea6d8a7dd84d36cbeaad93bb16f7e57eR1-R92): Moved OpenAI-specific code to a separate module implementing the common interface.

Configuration updates:

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959L6-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959L53-R64)

body:
The file drm-messagehandler.js contains configs for accessing licenses
from different drm servers for the key systems tested in wpt tests. This
test tries to load a persistent license into a temporary session and it
expects to fail, but for key systems that do not have an option to query
for persistent license because it isn't supported, the drm message
handler incorrectly returns a temporary license.

Now, we query the config, and if the config does not support querying
for the persistent-license sessiont type, we skip this test.

Tested via: `third_party/blink/tools/run_wpt_tests.py -t Default -p
chrome
third_party/blink/web_tests/external/wpt/encrypted-media/drm-temporary-license-type.https.html`

body: **Pull Request checklist** - [x] The commit(s) message(s) follows the contribution [guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) ? - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) ? - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ? From tests, we are finding that OTel Exponential histogram scale, bucketOffset and bucketCount can be volatile from sample to sample from same source. Frequently changing bucket scheme results in new chunk being created, and this can bleed at high scale. This PR creates a new vector ExpHistogramVector which stores the bucket definition along with each sample in the vector. During reads, we reuse the values array that stores bucket counts to avoid object allocation. E2E local test works. Optimizations done after benchmark. There was a performance hits were because of `Math.pow` due to reset of bucket scheme for each same. They have been optimized with pre computation and usage of `Math.exp`. ``` [info] Benchmark Mode Cnt Score Error Units [info] HistVectorBenchmark.ingestion thrpt 2 4100004.872 ops/s [info] HistVectorBenchmark.ingestionExpVector thrpt 2 4133372.497 ops/s [info] HistVectorBenchmark.queries thrpt 2 111176.203 ops/s [info] HistVectorBenchmark.queriesExpVector thrpt 2 108522.270 ops/s [info] Base2ExponentialHistogramQueryBenchmark.histQuantileRangeQueries thrpt 2 134.069 ops/s ``` Flame graph for hist-quantile benchmark Prior to the PR, with regular histogram vectors: ``` [info] Benchmark Mode Cnt Score Error Units [info] Base2ExponentialHistogramQueryBenchmark.histQuantileRangeQueries thrpt 2 135.804 ops/s ```

<!-- What did you change, and why? -->

Swapped out the 686KB `lodash` package for the tree-shakable `lodash-es`. Now it's only 123KB in the bundle, accounting for just 6.68% of the total app size, where it was 28.1% before.

I also simplified the imports, because now they can be tree-shaken. Importing submodules makes no difference to the bundle size.

Alterações propostas pelo PR

- Adiciona DTO's para remover a responsabilidade do Model, seguindo boas práticas de arquitetura em camadas (Layer Architecture)
- Adiciona **Mapper** para conversão entre **Model** e **DTO**
- Implementa os DTO's no Controller
- Implementa os DTO's no Service

Mudanças visam melhorar a organização do código, separando as responsabilidades e facilitando a manutenção e escalabilidade.
